otherDispositions.criterion: Dispositions must rest on the actual displayed labels and ordinary or taught meanings in both offered directions (docs/content-format.md:96-100,108-114): (a) with 唇 prompted, does the comparison card's displayed title name lips or a sense the 唇 card teaches or its cited sources attest for 唇/脣 (literary petal, Jitsu おどろく, old-dictionary ホトリ under 脣, noun しん labial sound)? (b) with the comparison card prompted, is lips a defensible answer for any of its ordinary senses? A comparison card's undisplayed secondary glosses matter only through (b) or where its displayed wording actually expresses them; GPT's caution that different titles alone do not dispose of secondary senses is preserved by requiring that explicit two-direction analysis with complete-source citations rather than a title-string comparison.
otherDispositions.boundedHarmless: GPT D8 片 is accepted as a source-based bounded harmless disposition: a sheet, leaf or one-of-a-pair relation is not a petal or lip meaning, and 花片 is a whole word, not a constituent sense (jmdict-families.xml:119-220; 02-extract.txt:14-27). Claude reached a compatible conclusion. No 唇/片 guard is required.
otherDispositions.sakuResolution: GPT D2's lexical distinction is accepted as correct: 咲く denotes a flower opening, while Daijisen defines the supplemental くちびる noun as 花びら (02-extract.txt:14-17; jmdict-families.xml:633-655). The separately accepted Q15 guard does not contradict it and is not a necessary-collision claim. It is a conservative label-consistency guard: the card already declares that flower is not a reliably wrong choice because of the petal sense, and the offered English label blossom; bloom carries no part-of-speech marker, so its noun reading (a flower; JMdict 1194500 groups blossom with petal at :140-146) sits in that same guarded answer space. The revised note must keep 咲く's verb meaning distinct from petal and lips.
otherDispositions.existingGuards: E1-E10 preserve 口, 花, 震, 動, 側, 辺, 際, 畔, 音 and 恐 as direct declarations on 唇 only; exclusions are symmetric and non-transitive. GPT L3's unrequested 境, 界, 岸 and 怖 remain conservatively declared without a complete E-style card-text validation in this pass.
otherDispositions.crossFamilyDisagreement: The other independent pass judged 声, 刃, 横, 郊, 危 and 響 harmless with label-based reasoning; GPT left them UNVERIFIED after fuller secondary-sense reads. Neither conclusion is adopted by default. Agreement or disagreement is corroboration, not proof.
otherDispositions.consistency: Q1 and Q12 deserve particular care: the candidate's own note guards unresolved broad side, edge, boundary or waterside labels. The author must state whether qualified labels such as cutting edge or outskirts fall outside that class, from sources, or guard them. No guard is required merely from a shared English stem.
